featured.title: RIP Replit
featured.description: A nostalgic homepage celebrating my early web projects with a polished, retro-inspired layout built entirely in HTML and CSS during my first year in the Web Design Pathways Program.
featured.reflection: This was one of my first serious CSS projects. Balancing nostalgia with modern structure taught me that playfulness and usability don't have to compete — you can have both if you're intentional about spacing and typography.

featured.title: Maple Leafs Site
featured.description: A fan site dedicated to the Toronto Maple Leafs featuring team stats, player highlights, and a bold hockey-inspired visual design.
featured.reflection: Designing around an existing brand taught me how to work within color and identity constraints while still making something that feels original and exciting.

featured.title: Little Bird Toys
featured.description: A cheerful e-commerce-style toy store site with product cards, playful colors, and a family-friendly shopping experience.
featured.reflection: Building a product-focused site made me think carefully about how people browse and discover items — white space and clear hierarchy matter a lot when selling something.

featured.title: Rock Paper Scissors
featured.description: A fully playable browser game with score tracking, randomized computer logic, and smooth animated state transitions between rounds. Built with vanilla JS.
featured.reflection: Writing game logic cleanly forced me to think about state before touching the DOM. I learned to separate data from display — a principle I still apply in every project.

featured.title: Client Website: HairByToni
featured.description: A real client portfolio site built for a local hair stylist — featuring elegant spacing, bold brand colors, a full services section, and clear appointment contact info.
featured.reflection: Designing around someone else's voice taught me to separate my personal taste from actual user need. The client had a clear personality — my job was to translate that into a site, not override it.

featured.title: Indiana College Recruitment
featured.description: A polished college recruitment website with a clean layout, clear calls-to-action, and modern content flow.
featured.reflection: This project sharpened my ability to present achievements and goals clearly for a college audience.

featured.title: Winter Shootout
featured.description: A competitive sports event website for a hockey's greatest event, featuring old/new goalies, old/new players, and a bold arena-ready visual style.
featured.reflection: Real-world event sites need to answer questions fast. This project pushed me to think about information architecture — what does someone need the moment they land on the page?
